subject: Post-demo: windowed token economics, streaming boundaries, and next steps
messages:
From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@lumoshealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; Rita Cheng <rita.cheng@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo notes + workload sketch (Lumos pilot)

Hi Lauren / team,

Thanks again for the demo — the performance tradeoffs you showed were helpful. Per our call, here's a concise sketch of the workload we need Redwood to qualify for the pilot:

- Objective: Support conversational triage + summarization for our clinician portal. Pilot is for US region, eventually multi-region.
- Typical request: user prompt + 2-3 system messages, expected generated output ~400-800 tokens (median ~600).
- Steady-state traffic: 18-25 QPS (office hours baseline).
- Hourly peaks: short bursts up to ~160-200 QPS for ~60-120s when several clinics open intake at once.
- Burst pattern: 4–6 bursts per day; heavy tail during 09:00–11:00 local time.
- Concurrency: ~40–80 concurrent sessions during peak; many of these use streaming partial responses for progress UI.
- Latency targets: first-token (stream start) p95 < 150 ms; end-to-end p95 < 350 ms for non-streamed; otherwise keep incremental chunk latency < 200 ms.
- KV / cache behavior: requests are partially stateful — many short-lived sessions where KV cache warms within the session but is not shared across unrelated users.
- Model mix: prefer a high-quality open model (16k context) with a quantized variant for cost-efficiency.

We've attached a 1-hour sample of representative traffic (CSV) and a draft SLA that lists our desired uptime and latency commitments.

Ask from our side: can you (1) confirm whether those latency targets are realistic for the given tokens/QPS mix on Redwood hosted, (2) advise on expected token/sec economic bandwidth for steady vs peak, and (3) propose a short list of model/config options (streaming-friendly, quantized) for sizing?

Thanks — happy to hop on a technical deep-dive if you need more detail.

—Evan

Attachments: lumos_traffic_sample_q3.csv (CSV, 42 KB); draft_sla_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + workload sketch (Lumos pilot)

Evan — thanks for the clear sketch and the sample. Looping in Marissa and Karthik for sizing and Sergio for SLA/ops commentary. A few quick clarifying questions so we scope the deep-dive effectively:

1) Peak window length: you indicated ~60–120s bursts. Can you confirm if the 160–200 QPS peaks are sustained for the full window or if they spike at the start of the window and decay (i.e., a ramp)?
2) Streaming behavior: are streamed responses long-running (multiple chunks over seconds) or short-lived (1–2 chunks, under 500 ms total)?
3) KV cache expectations: you said caches warm within a session. Do sessions reuse user-specific context across requests in the same session frequently (e.g., conversational turns every 5–10s)?
4) Model preference: do you have a hard requirement for 16k context now, or is 8k acceptable for the pilot if it substantially reduces cost?

Proposed next steps:
- If you can reply with the 60–120s window shape and streaming chunk profile, Marissa will run a quick bucketized token/sec and QPS sizing and share a preliminary capacity sketch (hosted + recommended Dedicated commit).
- Karthik will propose a test plan for validating first-byte p95 and sustained tokens/sec during a scaled run.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive this week to walk through sample traces and the CSV.

Quick timeline: Marissa will aim to circulate a sizing sketch by Tue (48 hours) once we have the clarifications.

—Lauren

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Miles <evan.miles@lumoshealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + workload sketch (Lumos pilot) — initial sizing sketch

Folks — I parsed the CSV and sketched three "bucketized" operating points to reflect the traffic shape Evan provided. Summary (prelim, hosted guidance):

- Inputs from sample: median request tokens ≈ 590, p75 ≈ 720, p95 ≈ 1,100. CSV shows peak instantaneous QPS spikes to ~175 for ~90s with a modest ramp up/down.

- Operating buckets (for cost & SLO mapping):
  * Steady: 20 QPS, 600 tokens/req -> ~12,000 tokens/sec sustained. Targeted first-byte p95 goal: 120–150 ms (hosted, warm KV).
  * Short peak: 90–120 QPS for ~3–5 minutes (aggregate sustained window of repeated smaller spikes) -> transient tokens/sec ~54k–72k. In these windows, batching efficiency improves but tail latency p95 may drift to ~300–450 ms unless we upsell reserved capacity or enable burst lanes.
  * Micro-burst: 160–200 QPS for 60–120s -> instantaneous tokens/sec 96k–120k. These are the hardest to meet for p95 first-byte without either (a) prewarmed reserved capacity, (b) model fallback to a lower-cost variant that meets latency, or (c) graceful degradation (reduce max tokens).

- Streaming specifics: CSV traces show ~60% of requests use streaming. Typical streamed sessions send 2–6 chunks over 400–900 ms total. That pattern favors a streaming-optimized kernel and small chunk sizes to maintain first-byte SLO.

- KV cache note: warm-within-session behavior helps steady-state but provides limited benefit during broad micro-bursts where unique user sessions dominate. We should assume cold starts across many concurrent sessions during peaks.

Initial sizing recommendations (hosted):
- For pilot (low-risk): provision for steady + short peak via hosted with a small Dedicated burst commit (recommended 2x steady QPS committed, plus burst capacity) — this hits p95 goals for steady and reduces risk in short peak windows.
- For guaranteed p95 during micro-bursts: recommend Dedicated reserved capacity sized to handle at least 70% of micro-burst tokens/sec, with fallback routing to a compatible quantized variant for the remainder.

Next steps (action items):
- Evan: confirm burst shape (sustained vs spike) and accept the proposed 45-min deep-dive.
- Lauren/Karthik: I'll assemble a preliminary cost delta table (hosted-only vs hosted + small Dedicated vs Dedicated-heavy) and include model variant tradeoffs (16k quantized, 8k quantized, 8k full-precision).
- Sergio: will map SLA language that reflects burst-mitigation behaviors and fallback policies.

I'll target sending the capacity sketch + cost delta by Tue 08 Sep EOD.

—Marissa

Attachments referenced: none (used CSV provided by Lumos).

Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + workload sketch (Lumos pilot) — confirming deep-dive

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. Quick answers:

- Burst shape: the 160–200 QPS windows are fairly sharp — ~20–30s ramp-up, ~60–120s near-peak, then a 30–60s decay. So your micro-burst framing is accurate.
- Streaming chunks: majority are short (2–4 chunks, ~250–700 ms total). A small subset (5–10%) are longer multi-chunk sessions tied to longer summaries.
- KV reuse: within a clinician session turns do occur every 6–12s for the same user. So per-session warm caching will help, but across users we expect many cold sessions during peaks.

We'd like the 45-min deep-dive on Wed 8 Sep at 10:00 AM PT if that works for the team — please send an invite and any pre-read (your sizing sketch + cost delta table).

We agree to the path: hosted pilot + small Dedicated burst commit as a starting point. Also open to a short performance validation run (10–15 minutes at scaled QPS) after the deep-dive to validate first-byte and tail p95.

—Evan
